ascari.polesWithFerrariNote: 13 of his 14 career poles came with Ferrari (1951-1953). Jolpica grid==1 on Ferrari entries, the Wikipedia results table (bold = pole) and Autosport's Ferrari pole ranking all give 13.

fangio.polesWithFerrariNote: All six came in his single Ferrari season, 1956. Jolpica grid==1 on Ferrari entries and the Wikipedia results table agree. In 1954 he drove for both Maserati and Mercedes (Jolpica lists both constructors for that title).

hawthorn.polesWithFerrariNote: All four career poles were with Ferrari in 1958 (Jolpica grid==1 and Wikipedia results table agree).

phil_hill.polesWithFerrariNote: All six career poles were with Ferrari (one in 1960, five in 1961); Jolpica grid==1 and Wikipedia results table agree.

surtees.polesWithFerrariNote: 1963 Italian GP, 1964 German and Italian GPs, 1966 Belgian GP. His other four career poles came with Lotus (1960), Lola (1962), Cooper (1966) and Honda (1968). Jolpica grid==1 and Wikipedia results table agree.

lauda.polesWithFerrariNote: 23 of his 24 career poles were with Ferrari (1974-1977); the other was the 1978 South African GP with Brabham. Jolpica, the Wikipedia results table and Autosport agree.

gilles_villeneuve.polesWithFerrariNote: 1979 United States GP West (Long Beach) and 1981 San Marino GP; both career poles were with Ferrari. Jolpica id is 'gilles_villeneuve' ('villeneuve' is Jacques).

scheckter.polesWithFerrariNote: 1979 Monaco GP. His other two career poles were with Tyrrell/Wolf. Jolpica grid==1 and Wikipedia results table agree.

mansell.polesWithFerrariNote: All three in 1990 (French, British and Portuguese GPs); none in 1989. Jolpica grid==1 and Wikipedia results table agree.

prost.polesWithFerrariNote: No poles in 1990-1991 with Ferrari (Jolpica grid==1 and Wikipedia results table agree), despite 5 Ferrari wins.

michael_schumacher.polesWithFerrariNote: 58 of 68 career poles were with Ferrari (1996-2006). Jolpica grid==1 on Ferrari entries and Autosport's Ferrari pole ranking both give 58. Jolpica qualifying data only begins in 2003, so the qualifying endpoint cannot cross-check the full count.

raikkonen.polesWithFerrariNote: Three in 2007, two in 2008, one each in 2017 and 2018. Jolpica grid==1, Jolpica qualifying P1 and Autosport all give 7.

alonso.polesWithFerrariNote: 2010 Italian and Singapore GPs, 2012 British and German GPs. Jolpica grid==1 and qualifying P1 both give 4; Wikipedia lists 2 poles each for the F10 and F2012 and 0 for the F138 and F14 T.

vettel.polesWithFerrariNote: 2015-2019. Jolpica grid==1, Jolpica qualifying P1 and Autosport all give 12.

sainz.polesWithFerrariNote: All six career poles were with Ferrari: 2022 British, Belgian and United States GPs, 2023 Italian and Singapore GPs, 2024 Mexico City GP. formula1.com and Jolpica grid==1 give 6. Jolpica qualifying P1 gives 5 because Verstappen was fastest in qualifying at the 2022 Belgian GP but took a grid penalty, so Sainz started from pole. The published figure (6) is used.

leclerc.polesWithFerrariNote: All 27 career poles are with Ferrari (none with Sauber in 2018, none so far in 2026). formula1.com and Jolpica grid==1 give 27. Jolpica qualifying P1 gives 24 because at the 2019 Mexico City, 2023 Belgian and 2024 Belgian GPs Verstappen set the fastest time but took a penalty, so Leclerc started from pole. The published figure (27) is used.

hamilton.polesWithFerrariNote: No Grand Prix pole with Ferrari so far (2025 to the 2026 Spanish GP). He has taken a sprint pole with Ferrari (2026 British GP sprint), but sprint poles are not counted. All 104 career Grand Prix poles came with McLaren and Mercedes. Jolpica qualifying P1 gives 107 career because of grid penalties; the published figure (104) is used.

moments: Finished third in the season-opening Australian Grand Prix on 8 March 2026, after he and George Russell swapped the lead several times in the opening laps.
Retired from the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix on 14 June 2026 with a power steering failure.

Won the British Grand Prix at Silverstone on 5 July 2026 from second on the grid. The race finished behind the Safety Car. It was his first win of 2026, the ninth of his career and Ferrari's 250th World Championship Grand Prix victory.
Finished third at the Chinese Grand Prix on 15 March 2026, his first Grand Prix podium for Ferrari.

Won the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix on 14 June 2026 from second on the grid. It was his first Grand Prix victory for Ferrari and the 106th of his career, and Russell and Norris joined him for the first all-British podium since 1968.
Took pole for the British Grand Prix sprint at Silverstone in July 2026, finished the sprint second, then finished third in the Grand Prix on 5 July.
Retired early from the Spanish Grand Prix at the Madring in Madrid on 13 September 2026 with a brake problem.
